unit: fractions of body height unless stated; metres
scope: Geometry for placing a simple player figure so the racket meets a given contact point. It shows reach and jump height only and carries no technique guidance.

reference.note: Segment lengths as fractions of body height H.
Maximum overall frame length and strung-area length and width. These Law 4 limits have not been re-read against the pinned PDF in this project; verify before relying on them.
Forehand jump smash, 18 regional to international male players.

eliteExample.note: Reachable height = player height + jump + racket length; Lin Dan example 1.78 + 0.7 + 0.65 m.

reference.note: "The interception point when smashing must be in front of the body."

jumpModel.note: Estimate countermovement jump height from sex, height, body mass and a self-rated level. Steps: (1) level -> cohort percentile jump at the cohort reference body; (2) convert to peak power with the Sayers equation; (3) scale power by fat-free mass, estimated from BMI with the Deurenberg equation at the cohort age (project assumption: power per kg fat-free mass is constant within a level); (4) convert back to jump height at the user body mass.

reference.note: Force-plate CMJ, hands on hips, best of two; US military officers aged 37 +/- 5. Fitter and older than typical learners, so treat as indicative.
Squat-jump equation fitted on 108 college-age men and women; SEE about 373 W.
Body fat % = 1.2 BMI + 0.23 age - 10.8 sex - 5.4 (sex: 1 male, 0 female).

overhead.note: An incoming shuttle counts as hittable overhead only if the straight arm points at least this far above horizontal at contact. Not from a source; a coach should confirm or change it.

movement.note: Reaction time and court sprint/lunge speed by fitness level. Reaction time includes visual recognition and initial weight shift.

openQuestions: Typical body height and jump height of the target learners.
Where the coach wants the body relative to the contact point for each stroke (the figure only uses straight-arm reach).
Jump norms for the target learners (the cohort used is older, fitter military officers); whether to scale the estimate down for untrained youth.
How the coach wants weak / average / good to map onto measured jumps.
Minimum arm elevation for an overhead contact (the shot lab assumes 45 degrees above horizontal).
